title: Escher's Cubes: Tiling the Faces of Polyhedra
summary: Isohedral or face-transitive polyhedra are polyhedra with identical faces, such that any face can be mapped onto any other via a symmetry of the polyhedron. Examples include the Platonic solids, Catalan solids, bipyramids, and trapezohedra. We use the orbit-counting theorem to count the number of ways of tiling the faces of such polyhedra up to their isometries given any arbitrary set of tile designs.
